newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's budget deficit narrows in November.
newsitem.headline: Israel's budget deficit narrows in November.

text.p: The Israeli government posted a budget deficit in November of 881 million shekels, excluding credits granted, preliminary figures released by the Treasury on Monday show.
Notes: Figures are in millions of shekels. Previous-month figures are final
The Treasury said the government had a deficit of 10.895 billion shekels in the first 11 months of the year, excluding credits granted, compared with a budgeted deficit of 7.609 billion shekels.
Officials said the full-year deficit was expected to reach 3.5 percent of gross domestic product, compared with the planned 2.5 percent.

Treasury officials will be using the latest figures to determine the exact size of the second-round of budget cuts to be presented to the cabinet next week. They said a final figure would probably be reached on Wednesday after a detailed report on November tax revenues is completed on Tuesday.
The Treasury is expected to propose cuts of between 1.5 billion and 2.3 billion shekels, on top of the 4.9 billion shekel cut contained in the original 1997 budget.
